Create a heatmap with square cells

Source: R/ggcalor.R
ggcalor.Rd

ggcalor() builds a heatmap as a grammar of cells. Cells are square by default and sized in millimetres, so the plot sizes itself instead of the device. The result is a ggplot object: add themes, scales, labels, and calor_*() verbs with +.

Usage

ggcalor(
  data,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  cell_size = 5,
  cell_gap = 0,
  cell_shape = c("square", "circle", "hex"),
  cell_radius = 0,
  cell_area = NULL,
  scale = c("none", "row", "column"),
  scale_method = c("zscore", "minmax"),
  mask = NULL,
  na_fill = "grey92",
  border = "white",
  palette = "auto",
  raster = c("auto", "never", "always"),
  raster_threshold = 20000,
  smooth = c("none", "contour", "raster"),
  smooth_sigma = 1,
  smooth_bins = 9,
  labels = c("both", "rows", "cols", "none"),
  label_position = c("auto", "top", "bottom")
)

Arguments

data

A numeric or categorical matrix, a wide data frame, or a long data frame (then give rows, cols, value). Categorical values get a discrete fill; clustering, ordering and margins then use presence (1/0).

rows, cols, value

Column names for long data. See calor_matrix().

cell_size

Cell size in millimetres. Give one number for square cells or c(width, height).

cell_gap

Gap between cells as a fraction of the cell (0 to 1).

cell_shape

"square", "circle" or "hex". Hexagons tile an offset lattice, so trees and tracks are not drawn with them.

cell_radius

Corner radius of square cells in millimetres.

cell_area

Optional matrix of the same shape whose values (scaled to 0 to 1) set each cell's area, for dot plots.

scale

Scale values by "row" or "column" before plotting, or "none".

scale_method

"zscore" or "minmax". See calor_scale().

mask

Optional logical matrix; TRUE cells are hidden (drawn as NA).

na_fill

Fill colour for missing or masked cells. Also applied to a fill scale you add, unless that scale sets its own na.value.

border

Colour of the cell border, or NA for none.

palette

"auto" picks a diverging palette when values span zero and a sequential one otherwise. Any scale_fill_*() can be added later to override.

raster

"auto" draws cells as a raster image when the matrix has more than raster_threshold cells, "always" or "never". Raster cells have no gap, border or shape.

raster_threshold

Cell count above which "auto" rasterises.

smooth

"none" draws cells. "contour" interpolates and blurs the matrix into a surface drawn as filled contour bands; "raster" draws the same surface as a continuous image. Dendrograms and tracks still align.

smooth_sigma

Blur radius in cells.

smooth_bins

Approximate number of contour bands; breaks are rounded to pretty values.

labels

Which labels to show: "both", "rows", "cols" or "none".

label_position

Where column labels go: "auto" (top, or bottom when a column dendrogram is present), "top" or "bottom".

Value

A ggplot object of class calor.

Examples

m <- matrix(rnorm(80), 10, 8, dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:10), paste0("s", 1:8)))
ggcalor(m, cell_size = 6)

ggcalor(m, scale = "row") + calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE, k = 3)
